paragraphs.text: Stirling Mk IV LK116 'A' of 620 Squadron flew from RAF Great Dunmow on 20 March 1945 on a training supply-dropping exercise to RAF Great Sampford. An unidentified Luftwaffe intruder attacked it, and it crashed by the River Chelmer at Ford Farmhouse, Great Dunmow. The inscription on the memorial says the resulting fire brought the aircraft down in the fields behind Oakroyd Avenue.

Seven men were aboard. Flight Sergeant Cramp baled out and survived. The other six were killed: Squadron Leader George Whitty, DFC (pilot), Warrant Officer John Williams (navigator), Pilot Officer George Ames (wireless operator), Warrant Officer Andrew Bell, RCAF (air gunner), Flight Sergeant George Douglas (bomb aimer) and Captain George Slater, who was a passenger.

Slater was the SAS headquarters liaison officer attached to RAF Great Dunmow. Bell had already evaded capture in France in July 1944, after the loss of a 190 Squadron Stirling, before he joined 620 Squadron.

The memorial is an incised slate tablet on a stand, at the corner of a house driveway in Oakroyd Avenue, Great Dunmow. The IWM register records its condition as good. The inscription ends '(3 NAMES)', although six men died.

notes: CONTRADICTS OUR RECORD: record and IWM say died 3 / 3 names / 'no other survivors' beyond Cramp; CASPIR (S3) and Aircrew Remembered (S10), two publishers, say six killed and one survivor (seven aboard). Names on the stone are not in the IWM page, so which three are named is unknown; names_on_memorial=4 in our record also unexplained (IWM: commemorated 4, died 3, served 1). I did not claim IWM's 3 as died_count because it would out-rank the researched sources and be accepted. Decision for Keith. Custodian: IWM maintainer, erected-by, maker and dedication fields are blank; nothing found in searches. Memorial sits at the corner of a house driveway (IWM), so a private householder may be involved: not investigated. Ames: IBCC page returned 404 to my fetch, so his rank, number and date rest on a search-result summary of that page plus CASPIR; age, burial and CWGC link not found. Whitty's CASPIR page is internally inconsistent on burial (own entry Brookwood, crew table 'unknown'); CWGC settles Brookwood. Cramp: only initial 'A' known (CASPIR); rank from inscription/CASPIR; role flight engineer and landing at Barnston come only from Remember the Fallen (community tier, held back; it also cites Sandra Taylor's research and Mark Rogers' 1999 book). Aircrew Remembered calls the attacker a night fighter; others say intruder. ASN wikibase 161626 (reported via search: 6 killed of 7, flight engineer survived) could not be fetched (cert error/403), not used. CASPIR is one publisher (S3 and S4 count once). Slater nationality not stated; Paradata says born in South Africa, not claimed. A second Paradata page reportedly describes his death only as a UK training exercise: not fetched. Other Dunmow Stirling memorials (LK276 bench at Newton Green, 190 Squadron) are a different crash.
